citation: Bowles, Reed, Ringgenberg and Thornock (2024), Anomaly Time, Journal of Finance 79(5) (lit [29]); Engelberg, McLean and Pontiff (2018), Anomalies and News, Journal of Finance 73(5) (lit [28]); the fast rate is Y-5's registered two_speed_fast_theta (atx-engine/include/atx/engine/book/two_speed.hpp; Ruling W3-16)
claim: anomaly returns are concentrated in the first month after a firm's information release and decay soon after; stale formation understates predictability (Bowles et al.); anomaly returns are several times higher on earnings days (Engelberg et al.; lit section 2.3)
source_sample_basis: Bowles et al. (the rule's own source, the published sample): 'Our sample period begins January 1990 and goes through 2019' (read in the first AL-CLOCK session, handoff-AL-CLOCK.md); Engelberg et al. is a supporting citation, not the primary source (PRE-19)
source_sample_flag: FLAGGED under PRE-19 / PRE-31 (Ruling ALCLOCK-2: the primary source's sample ends 2015 or later); P9-C stays registered (PRE-14 unchanged); the clean-source book of the OD-3 read applies no info-clock-rate-v1
predicted_mechanism: anomaly returns arrive in the month after a firm's information release, so a name moved toward its aim at the fast rate in the 21 sessions after its latest earnings announcement's reaction session holds more of the signal while it still pays; the total trade toward a step change is unchanged, only its participation per day rises
house_form: a NAV trade-rate rule: aim-partial-v5's per-name rate vector (the per-name-v1 seam of strategy_target_replay aim_partial_weights), formed once per rebalance decision from the role field ea_days_since (atx-impl book/nav_decide.cpp nav_info_clock_rates; strategy_nav_replay.hpp states it); NAV flag --rate info-clock-rate-v1, no parameter

constants.name: theta_fast
constants.value: two_speed_fast_theta(C) = 1 - 2^(-C/5) at the rebalance cadence C (.12945 at C = 1, .5 at C = 5)
constants.why: Y-5's registered fast rate (two-speed-v1: half of an aim gap closes in 5 sessions at any cadence); Ruling W3-16: the function, not the literal .12945, which is its cadence-1 value (lit section 2.3)

constants.name: theta_slow
constants.why: the parent's aim-partial-v5 theta (two_speed_slow_theta); the NAV exe refuses the rule at any other --trade-fraction

constants.name: window_sessions
constants.why: Bowles et al.'s one month after the information release (21 sessions); the window is closed: 0 and 21 are fast

constants.name: field
constants.why: the house's event clock: sessions since the reaction session of the name's latest visible primary earnings announcement (atx-engine/tools/research_fields_sec.py, recipe sec-ea-days-since-reaction-v1; >= 0, NaN without a fresh announcement)

fixed_choices: the paper's information-release date is mapped to the reaction session of the name's latest visible primary earnings announcement as the role field ea_days_since records it (t minus that session: session_date for pre-market, intraday and closed-day releases, the next session for post-market; NaN without a fresh announcement): a FIXED CHOICE of this registration (Ruling ALCLOCK-2), made before any read; no other release (10-K / 10-Q filing, news) enters the clock; the published sample is the one a reader can check
member i at rebalance decision d moves theta_fast when ea_days_since[d, i] lies in [0, 21], else theta_slow; a NaN clock is slow; the clock is read at row d only (causal)
the aim (L x desired), the dust band and the exit rule are the parent's; a nonmember is never moved by theta (its exit applies) and gets the slow rate in the vector
one rate vector per decision for every book, formed on the calling thread before the books' DECIDE, so --book-workers N runs (the bytes of one worker; InfoClockRate.BookWorkersOneAndFourSameBytes)
the book's one rate rule: per-name-v1, two-speed-v1, aim-partial-v6 and the spo rules are refused with it (the row's incompatible[]); the parent must run --rule aim-partial-v5 at --trade-fraction .05

Ruling ALCLOCK-3: --capacity-curve is accepted with this rate (it reads no NAV, so each capacity book moves at the members' clock rates as the main books do); per-name-v1 stays refused with the capacity curve and aim-partial-v6 refuses every non-fixed rate, this one included (InfoClockRate.CapacityCurveAcceptsThisRateOnly)
a construction-grid variant keeps the base cadence under the rule (the fast rate is formed once per decision at it)

the field is pinned through the run's --fields manifest (point in time; recorded in the recipe's financing_fields.fields_used under the rule); a manifest without it, or a cell outside NaN-or-finite->=0, is refused before any output
the decide (deploy) path keeps refusing every non-fixed rate: the rule is a replay rule in P9
realised_leverage: Ruling C3-4: the rule changes only the per-name rate, never L or the aim. Per name the step is convex (|w_next| <= max(|w|, L |desired|)); with one rate for every name the planned gross stays within max(the book's gross, gross(aim)), but unequal rates can carry it above gross(aim) in a rotation (fast names fill toward new aims while slow names still unwind). Cap stated for the rule: planned gross <= (theta_fast / theta_slow) x gross(aim) by contraction, outside the dust band (2.589 x at cadence 1); loose. In P9-C the cell is gross-matched (gross_match pm6-6-engine): the match stage solves L' so that the cell's realised mean gross equals its parent's within C2's tolerance, so the realised gross the OD5-7 cap reads is the parent's; the daily realised gross is printed by the NAV exe (daily CSV) beside it
restatement: Ruling DEC-16 (blind, before any Y read): distinct from Y-5 and R-3. Y-5 (two-speed-v1) buckets THEMES into a fast and a slow sleeve, each with its own aim and holdings, netted into one trade; this rule keeps one aim and one book and sets a rate per NAME-DAY from an event clock (the name's earnings announcement), whatever theme its alpha comes from: another decision unit (name-day vs theme) and another object (a rate vector vs sleeve aims; no sleeve, no netting). R-3 is a per-signal aim gain at one rate. Cost if wrong: one restated trial (N_c +1)
print_opt_in: Ruling ALCLOCK-1: --info-clock-print (NavSpec options.info_clock_print) is print-only, not a rule flag and owned by no K-P9-7 row: it loads ea_days_since from --fields without recording it in the recipe and adds to each scenario of summary.json the block info_clock (rate, field {name, sha256}, window_sessions, theta_fast, theta_slow, name_days, fast_name_days, missing_name_days, fast_share, planned_turnover, fast_planned_turnover, turnover_share, definition) at whatever rate the book runs; flag absent = every byte of before; the rule alone prints no block. P9-C and its reference name it alike (root on the Y-F0 reference at the wave-3 P9-B0; the cell inherits it)

predictions.registered_before_any_read: the fast-rate share of name-days and the planned-turnover share on fast name-days are printed for the cell and its parent by the same C++ producer (info_clock block under --info-clock-print on both); the OD-3 prediction: turnover share up and gross up against the parent (plan section 5.3); the total traded quantity toward a step change is unchanged, participation per day rises on fast name-days (lit section 2.3)
predictions.expected_effect: +.02 to +.06 net Sharpe [est]; book gross +~5% [est]; capacity down (plan section 7.2; lit section 2.3)
